notes: ROBOTS: https://www.zarahome.com/robots.txt fetched FIRST, before any other request on the host. NO Claude agent is named anywhere in it - there is no 'User-agent: ClaudeBot', 'anthropic-ai' or 'Claude-Web' group, and no Content-Signal line. The named-bot groups are HTTrack, Slurp, MJ12bot, AmazonProductDiscoverybot and AmazonProductBot (all 'Disallow: /') plus proximic ('Disallow: /itxrest/*'). We fall under 'User-agent: *', which does NOT disallow /es/ or /itxrest/ - only proximic is barred from /itxrest/*. The '*' disallows cover checkout/account/wishlist, /*search.html*, /*share*, /*shop-the-look*, the /ki /ax /wa /wy /wz /we /wm /xx /xy /ru stores, secondary-language paths INCLUDING '/es/en/*' (so the English ES storefront is off-limits and every URL here is the Spanish /es/ form), *hidden/*, *contact-swatches*, and a parameter list (pricePrecedence, catalogId, isMobile, modeView, gclid, keyWord, dir, wedding, keyWordCatentry, subid, epik, y_source, parentId) that does NOT include celement. No Crawl-delay is declared; probe.py's 2s per-host pacing plus explicit sleeps were used throughout. ACCESS - HONEST ACCOUNT: every HTML page on www.zarahome.com (home page, /es/, and every /es/<slug>-nNNNN PLP) is served an Akamai Bot Manager JS interstitial - a 2.2 KB stub with a meta-refresh to ?bm-verify=..., an /interstitial/ic.html iframe and a POST to /_sec/verify?provider=interstitial. That is an ACCESS obstacle, NOT a robots exclusion, and the two are not conflated here. I worked the documented fallback ladder: (1) all ten curl_cffi fingerprints in probe.PROFILES individually (chrome120/124/131, edge101, firefox133, safari15_5/17_0/17_2_ios/18_0/18_0_ios) - all ten returned the interstitial; (2) a persistent curl_cffi Session with es-ES Accept-Language, Referer and Upgrade-Insecure-Requests on /es/ then the PLP - interstitial; (3) the r.jina.ai reader prefix - HTTP 403; (4) trailing-slash, /es (no slash), /ww/es/ and ?ajax=true variants - all interstitial. I did NOT attempt to solve or circumvent the bot-detection challenge. (5) The rung that worked: the site's own sitemap and API hosts, which are NOT behind the interstitial and are robots-permitted for us. https://www.zarahome.com/8/info/sitemaps/sitemap-index-home-categories-zh.xml -> sitemap-home-categories-zh-es-0.xml.gz (1,665 URLs, 332 of them Spanish /es/ category URLs) returned 200 on the first try, and the Inditex storefront APIs /itxrest/... and /api/storefront/... answer plain 200 JSON with no cookie, no session and no challenge. STORE (discovered, not assumed): /itxrest/2/catalog/store/<id> was walked over 84009900-84009959 and returns each store's own identity document. 84009900 = countryCode ES, countryName 'España', storeDefaultLanguageId -5 (Español, es_ES), catalogs[type 1] = {id: 80290093, identifier 'ZH_ONT_ES_SEASON'}. This is a genuinely separate Inditex catalogue from Zara Home UK/SR 90 (84009906 / 80290024 'ZH_UK_SEASON') and from Zara Home DE/SR 106 (84009904 / 80290000 'ZH_POZ_NOR_SEASON'), so this is the ES storefront's own assortment, not a sibling's. Language -5 (Spanish) was used for every call so the node names and slugs are the Spanish ones. TREE: the storefront's own category tree, /itxrest/2/catalog/store/84009900/80290093/category?languageId=-5&appId=1 (1.26 MB, 687 nodes walked), cross-checked node-for-node against the rendered mega-menu /api/storefront/1/stores/84009900/menu?language=es-ES&clientId=web-zh&catalogId=80290093. The two agree EXACTLY for the BAÑO department (id 1089013, categoryUrl bano-n1050): same 24 children in the same order, including the four 'empty' spacer nodes, which were dropped. Every slug comes from the node's own categoryUrl field - none was guessed - and every recorded slug was additionally confirmed present in the site's published ES category sitemap. I also keyword-swept all 687 nodes for baño|bath|espejo|mirror|toalla|towel|ducha|shower|inodoro|toilet|lavabo|basin|sink|jabon|soap|grifo|tap|vanit|neceser|albornoz|alfombra (68 hits), which surfaced the bathroom content filed OUTSIDE the BAÑO department: MUEBLES > BAÑO (bathroom furniture, recorded), MUEBLES > PERCHEROS Y TOALLEROS (already in Furniture.xlsx), NIÑOS Y BEBÉS > BAÑO and > BEBÉS > Baño, SPECIAL PRICES > BAÑO, LAVANDERÍA > CESTAS Y ORGANIZACIÓN, FRAGANCIAS > JABONES Y CREMAS and DECORACIÓN > ESPEJOS - all handled in review[]. Zara Home is a textiles-and-accessories retailer: it sells no baths, toilets, basins, taps, showers or enclosures, so rules 4-8 have no nodes on this storefront. DUPLICATE-SLUG RULE (derived from the data, and load-bearing): several nodes share one categoryUrl. In every collision exactly ONE node has categoryUrlParam == null and the others carry categoryUrlParam == their own id - i.e. the null node owns the bare slug and the others need ?celement=<id>. Examples: bano-cajas-n3886 is owned by BAÑO > ALMACENAJE (1020708636) while ACCESORIOS DE BAÑO > Cajas y botes (1020447630) needs the param; bano-cestas-cajas-n4142 is owned by BAÑO > ALMACENAJE > Cestas (1020708638) while LAVANDERÍA > CESTAS Y ORGANIZACIÓN and DORMITORIO > VESTIDOR > Organización need it; bano-n1050 is owned by BAÑO > BAÑO (1020704134), not by the department node. Two independent confirmations: Final.xlsx already records this storefront with exactly that URL form (/es/en/lighting-lamps-cordless-n5192?celement=1020692636), and the Zara Home UK pass independently observed the bare bano-cajas slug rendering STORAGE rather than Cosmetic Storage. ONLY nodes that own their bare slug outright were put in rows[]; every ?celement-dependent node was put in review[] instead. QTY: Zara Home publishes no 'N artículos' / 'Mostrando 1-N de M' header anywhere on the site, and numberOfProducts is null for every node in the category tree, so there is no rendered total to read. The quantity is therefore an EXHAUSTIVE ENUMERATION of the node's own grid - the unique ccIds returned by the endpoint the PLP itself renders from, /itxrest/3/catalog/store/84009900/80290093/category/<id>/product?languageId=-5&appId=1&showProducts=true&showNoStock=false&withSubCategories=false. That endpoint returns the whole grid in one response (no pagination), so counting it IS enumeration to exhaustion, not a header taken on trust.
